We need to find a retrosynthetic template that when applied to target molecule (C=C(C1=CC=C(OC)C=C1)C2=CC=C(OC)C=C2) gives a precursor (mapped_rxn) and template_id. The reaction is Peterson: formation of alkene from beta-hydroxy silane elimination. In retrosynthesis, we break C=C double bond to give a beta-hydroxy silane precursor (i.e., an alcohol with SiMe3 attached to carbon adjacent to carbonyl? Actually Peterson: alpha-silyl carbanion adds to carbonyl forming beta-hydroxy silane, then elimination gives alkene. So forward: carbonyl + silyl carbanion -> beta-hydroxy silane -> alkene. In retrosynthesis, we break alkene to give carbonyl and silyl carbanion? But the description: new C=C formed, while C-Si and C-O broken. So forward: C-C double formed, C-Si broken, C-O broken. So retrosynthetic step: break C=C into C-Si and C-O bonds, forming a carbonyl (ketone) and a silyl group attached to carbon (maybe as silyl carbanion). The target molecule is a stilbene derivative with two anisole rings (methoxy). The double bond is between two aromatic carbons each attached to anisole ring. So the precursor would be a carbonyl (maybe a ketone) attached to SiMe3? Actually the double bond is between two sp2 carbons each attached to aromatic ring. The beta-hydroxy silane intermediate would be something like Ar-CH(OH)-SiMe3 attached to other aryl? Wait typical Peterson: R2C=CR2 from carbonyl R2C=O + R3SiCH2- (silyl carbanion) gives beta-hydroxy silane R2C(OH)-CH2-SiR3 then elimination gives alkene. So the carbonyl carbon becomes the carbon bearing OH and SiR3 attached to it, then elimination yields double bond between that carbon and the carbon originally bearing the carbanion. So in our case, the double bond is between two aryl-substituted carbons. So the carbonyl precursor would be an aryl ketone (aryl-CO-aryl?) Actually carbonyl carbon becomes the carbon bearing OH and SiR3. So the carbonyl is attached to one aryl group, and the carbanion is attached to the other aryl group. So precursor: aryl-CO-CH2-SiMe3? Wait the carbonyl carbon is attached to aryl (Ar-CO-). The carbanion carbon is attached to other aryl (Ar-CH2-). After addition, we get Ar-CO-CH(OH)-SiMe3 attached to other aryl? Actually the addition of silyl carbanion to carbonyl yields a beta-hydroxy silane where the carbonyl oxygen becomes OH, and the carbanion carbon attaches to carbonyl carbon. So product: Ar-CH(OH)-CH2-SiMe3 where the first carbon is the former carbonyl carbon attached to aryl, second carbon is the carbanion carbon attached to SiMe3. Then elimination yields Ar-CH=CH-Ar (stilbene) plus SiMe3-OH? Actually elimination removes SiMe3 and OH to give alkene and SiMe3-OH? The eliminated groups are SiMe3 and OH combine to give SiMe3-OH (trimethylsilanol). So the broken bonds: C-O (the carbonyl C=O becomes C-O in beta-hydroxy) then broken to give C=O? Wait forward: C-O broken (the carbonyl C=O becomes C-O in beta-hydroxy then eliminated). In retrosynthesis, we need to add C-O and C-Si to form the alkene.

Thus the precursor likely is a ketone (aryl-CO-CH2-SiMe3) with the other aryl attached to the carbonyl carbon? Actually the double bond is between two aryl-substituted carbons, each carbon attached to an aryl ring. So the carbonyl would be aryl-CO-CH2-SiMe3 where the CH2 is attached to the other aryl? Wait the carbonyl carbon is attached to one aryl, the other carbon (carbanion) attached to the other aryl. So the precursor is Ar-CO-CH2-SiMe3 where the CH2 is attached to the other aryl? That would be Ar-CO-CH2-SiMe3 with the CH2 also attached to second aryl? That would be a benzylic carbon attached to both aryl and SiMe3 and carbonyl? Actually CH2 cannot have three substituents. So maybe the carbonyl is a diaryl ketone (Ar-CO-Ar). Then the silyl carbanion adds to carbonyl carbon, giving a beta-hydroxy silane where the carbon bearing OH is attached to both aryl groups and SiMe3? That seems plausible: Starting ketone: Ar-CO-Ar (a diaryl ketone). Add silyl carbanion (SiMe3-CH2-) to carbonyl carbon, giving Ar-C(OH)(CH2SiMe3)-Ar (beta-hydroxy silane). Then elimination yields Ar-CH=CH-Ar (stilbene) plus SiMe3-OH? Actually elimination would involve removal of SiMe3 and OH from same carbon, forming double bond between that carbon and the adjacent carbon (the CH2). The adjacent carbon is the CH2 attached to SiMe3. So the double bond forms between carbonyl carbon (now bearing OH) and the CH2 carbon (bearing SiMe3). So product is Ar-CH=CH-Ar. Yes that matches.

Thus retrosynthetic step: target stilbene -> diaryl ketone + trimethylsilyl carbanion (or silyl reagent). But template likely expects precursor as a carbonyl (ketone) and a silyl reagent? However the template likely maps to a reaction where a carbonyl and a silyl carbanion produce alkene. In retrosynthesis, we break alkene into carbonyl and silyl group attached to carbon (maybe as a silyl reagent). The mapped_rxn should be something like "C=C(C1=CC=C(OC)C=C1)C2=CC=C(OC)C=C2>>O= C(C1=CC=C(OC)C=C1)C2=CC=C(OC)C=C2.[Si]"? Not sure.

We need to search template catalog with criteria: functional_groups_broken includes "trimethylsilyl"? Actually broken groups: ketone and trimethylsilyl are lost. So functional_groups_broken = ["ketone","trimethylsilyl"]; functional_groups_formed = ["alkene"]. Also bonds broken: C-O (carbonyl) and C-Si. Bonds formed: C=C. Let's try search.
